Experiment_Name: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids II)
Key_Findings: Thick solid fuels require sustained external heat flux to maintain burning in microgravity and show narrow burning regimes near extinction; self-extinction can occur at low airflow but is not guaranteed across all geometries and oxygen levels.
AI_Summary: Thick plastic components are harder to sustain burning in space — but self-extinction is not guaranteed, and NASA's guide notes this is a common misconception.
Safety_Recommendations: Use thick, high-density structural polymers where possible; do not rely on airflow shutoff alone to suppress a fire.
